Use this guide to find Ignite sessions and labs, meet the teams behind each, and start thinking about the organizational questions you want to bring to the conference. Bookmark this post at aka.ms/IntuneAtIgnite so you can find it again.
Featured sessions

new.title: Recommended privacy permissions for Mac
new.text:
The Privacy Library Item's Recommended privacy permissions area now supports Mac, in addition to iPhone and iPad. Admins can recommend app permissions for macOS apps and website permissions for Safari, so end users see a single consent prompt listing everything an app or site needs instead of being prompted one permission at a time. The user can select Allow to grant every recommended permission at once, or Not Now, in which case the app continues to prompt for individual permissions as it normally would.
Supported Mac app permissions include Bluetooth, Camera, Dictation, Local Network, Location, and Microphone. Mac apps are identified by bundle ID and code requirement, and a recommendation applies only when the installed app's code signature matches. Website rules use the same specific and wildcard domains as iPhone and iPad. This requires Macs on macOS 27 or later.
For more details, see Configure the Privacy Library Item.

new.title: Windows Local Account Management in Hexnode UEM: A Step-by-Step Guide
new.text:
What Is Windows Local Account Management?
Windows local account management is the process of creating, configuring, securing, and removing user accounts stored directly on individual Windows devices.
On shared workstations and kiosk-style devices, manual account administration can create inconsistent privileges and leave orphaned accounts after employee offboarding. With Windows unified endpoint management (UEM), IT admins can manage local accounts remotely across multiple devices instead of configuring each device individually.
A local account is defined on an individual Windows device, which acts as its security authority. A domain account normally authenticates against an organizational directory service and may have permissions to access local and domain resources.
Windows can allow offline sign-in when a domain controller is unavailable. This requires valid cached domain credentials and enabled credential caching. However, users cannot access network resources that require domain validation until the domain controller becomes available.
An administrator account can perform privileged system tasks, change settings, and manage other users. In contrast, a standard account supports routine activities with fewer privileges, reducing unnecessary administrative access.

new.title: Bug fix for Home screen & kiosk mode and "Unlimited" VPP licenses for free apps
new.text:
In this article
Toggle
Home screen & kiosk mode fix (Android)
We fixed an issue where deploying a Home screen & kiosk mode configuration profile with the Kiosk mode with 1 app configuration type could cause some Android devices to flash repeatedly and briefly exit kiosk lockdown. Kiosk mode with 1 app now starts reliably and stays active, including after a device reboot.
The fix is delivered via a Miradore client update. We recommend updating the Miradore client app on all your managed Android devices to version 2.18.12 (Build 475), even if you have not seen this issue. Keeping the client up to date ensures you have the latest fixes and improvements.
“Unlimited” shown for free VPP apps and books (iOS and iPadOS)
From October 22, 2026, Apple moves free apps and books in Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager to an unlimited license model. Miradore now shows "Unlimited" for these apps and books instead of a very large number (2147483647).
What changes in the Miradore UI:
The VPP licenses column is renamed "Used VPP licenses" and now shows used / total instead of available / total. For free apps, the total shows "Unlimited" (for example, "5 / Unlimited"). This applies to the application list (Management > Applications), the Assign VPP license wizard on the user page, and the Assign VPP license dialog on the device page.
On the application version page, the Assign VPP license dialog and its confirmation step show "Unlimited" as the available license count.
On the application version page, the License status section shows the number of assigned licenses and "Unlimited" available for free apps, instead of the pie chart. Paid apps keep the pie chart.
Sorting and filtering by license count still work. Unlimited sorts as the highest value, and filtering with "Unlimited" finds free apps.
License availability checks never block assigning an unlimited app or book.
Paid apps and books keep their numeric license counts and behave as before, apart from the column change to used / total.
Notice that this is a UI change only. The Miradore API v1 and reporting data continue to return the raw value provided by Apple (2147483647) for unlimited licenses.

changed.text:
SureAccess Configuration Guide for macOS and Windows
1. Overview
Use this guide to configure SureAccess in SureMDM for macOS and Windows devices. You can configure the VPN connection, control website access, block specific URLs, and manage data uploads through Domain-Based and Application-Based DLP policies.
Supported Agent Versions
Web Protection and Data Protection settings in SureAccess are supported on devices running the following minimum agent versions. Ensure that the installed agent meets or exceeds the specified version to access and use these settings.
Windows: Agent version 2.6.3 or later
macOS: Agent version 3.0.9 or later
2. Configuration Flow
3. Configure the SureAccess Payload
Step 1: Open the Profile Configuration
Sign in to the SureMDM console.
Navigate to Profiles.
Select the platform for which you want to configure SureAccess: macOS or Windows.
Select the Enrollment Type if macOS is selected
Locate the SureAccess payload and click Configure.
Important for Windows: A profile containing a VPN Configuration payload cannot also be configured with the SureAccess payload. Remove the conflicting payload before proceeding, if required.
Step 2: Configure VPN Settings
In the SureAccess payload, open the VPN section and configure the available settings according to your organization's requirements.
SettingAdministrator Action
Enable SureAccess
When enabled, deploys the SureAccess agent and applies secure remote access settings. When disabled, removes the configuration.
Connection Name
Enter the name to identify the connection.
Always On
Keeps the SureAccess connection active at all times.
Tunnelled CIDR List
Select the IP ranges (CIDR blocks) that should be accessed through SureAccess. DNS Resolutions are skipped for this IP range and are accessible over IP addresses only.
Tunnelled FQDN List
Select the FQDNs that will be routed through the SureAccess tunnel.
Enable Authentication
Enables user authentication during SureAccess setup.
Review the connection settings before moving to Web & Data Protection.
4. Configure Web & Data Protection
Expand Web & Data Protection in the SureAccess payload.
Enable Enable Protection Policies.
Configure the required protection modules:
Web Content Filtering
Blocked URLs
DLP Configuration
5. Configure Web Content Filtering
Use Web Content Filtering to control website access based on website categories.
Steps
Under Web & Data Protection, open Web Content Filtering.
Enable Enable Protection Policies, if it is not already enabled.
Select the required Filtering Mode:
Allow Websites — allow websites in the selected categories and restrict others.
Block Websites — block websites in the selected categories.
Select the required categories, such as:
Online Ads
Pornography / Sexually Explicit / Adult Content
Social Networking
Popup Ads
Unknown
If you need to identify a website's category, use the AskDeepthought lookup option, where available.
Review the selected mode and categories.
Note: Select the filtering mode carefully. The selected mode determines how the category selection is applied.
6. Configure Blocked URLs
Use this section to block specific websites or domains regardless of the category-filtering configuration.
Steps
Expand Blocked URLs.
Click Add.
Select the required input method:
Enter Manually — enter the URLs or domains to block.
Choose from FQDN List — select entries from the available FQDN resources.
Import CSV — import a supported file containing the URLs.
Enter or select the required entries, or upload the file.
Review the entries and resolve any invalid or duplicate values as indicated by the console.
Save the entries.
To maintain the list later, use the available Edit, Delete, and Search options. Multiple entries can be selected for deletion.
To manage reusable FQDN resources, navigate to:
Settings → Account Settings → Enterprise Integration → SureAccess → SureAccess Configurations → FQDN Resources

changed.title: windows cli enrollment
changed.text:
Windows CLI Based Enrollment
Windows CLI (Command Line Interface)–based enrollment enables administrators to onboard Windows devices into SureMDM using command-line instructions. This method supports automated and standardized enrollment by allowing administrators to deploy enrollment commands through scripts or enterprise deployment mechanisms such as Group Policy Objects (GPO), device management tools, or other MDM solutions.
CLI-based enrollment supports bulk device onboarding and migration scenarios while enabling a zero-touch setup experience. This ensures consistent device configuration and reduces manual intervention during the enrollment process.
Supported Versions
Windows 10
Windows 11
Prerequisites
‘CLI Based Enrollment’ is supported on Windows devices with SureMDM Agent Version 6.22.0 and later.
To enroll Windows devices using CLI, follow the steps below:
Step 1: Navigate to Windows Enrollment
Login to the SureMDM Web Console.
Navigate to: Enrollment > Manual Enrollment > Windows > CLI Based Enrollment
Step 2: Configure Enrollment Settings
Click Configure to customize enrollment settings.
The Enrollment Configuration window appears.
Enter the required configuration details:
Enrollment ConfigurationDescription
Enrollment Group Path
Specifies the group in the SureMDM console where the device will be enrolled.
Device Name Type
Select the naming method for Windows devices. The selected option will be used as the device's assigned name. Select from one of the following options:
Use Mac Address
Use System Generated BIOS Name
Use Device Host Name
Use Product Serial Number
SureMDM Agent URL
Select the source for the SureMDM Agent. Choose ‘Latest SureMDM Agent’ to use the most recent version, or ‘Custom’ to specify your own agent URL.
Custom SureMDM Agent URL
Enter the complete URL where SureMDM Agent is hosted, This option appears when ‘Custom’ is selected as an option in ‘SureMDM Agent URL’ dropdown.
Download Path
Enter the complete UNC path where the file will be downloaded. Ensure to include the full folder path, file name, and file extension.
Step 3: Apply Configuration
After entering the required details, click Apply.
Once the configuration is applied, the CLI enrollment command will be generated and displayed in an encoded format.
Click Copy Command to copy the generated command.
Step 4: Execute CLI Command on Windows Device
Open Command Prompt or PowerShell on the target Windows device.
Paste the copied enrollment command and press Enter to start the enrollment process.
The SureMDM Agent will be downloaded, installed, and configured automatically.
note
Upon running above CLI command, the enrollment process will be zero-touch for Users with Admin privileges, while Standard users will be prompted to enter admin credentials to install the SureMDM agent.
If Enrollment Authentication Type is set to Require Password under Account Settings > Device Enrollment Rules, the generated CLI command includes the configured password, so end users won't be prompted to enter it during enrollment. To enforce password authentication during CLI-based enrollment, we recommend you to contact our Support for removing the password parameter from the CLI command.
Step 5: Verify Enrollment Status
Once the command execution completes:
The device will appear in the Device Grid in the SureMDM Web Console.
The device status will change to Online once the SureMDM Agent establishes communication with the server.
note
Network restrictions or proxy configurations may impact agent download and installation.
If using automation tools or scripts, verify that the command is executed in a silent or unattended mode as required.

new.title: Scalefusion October 16th, 2026 Release Notes
new.text:
Version Information
Scalefusion Dashboard: v68.3.0
Release Notes
1. Compliance Reports
Compliance Reports have been enhanced and are now available to customers based on their plan. IT Administrators can generate reports based on OS version, application version, and encryption status to evaluate device compliance against defined conditions. Supported compliance criteria include:
a. OS Version: Generate compliance reports for Android, iOS, Windows, and macOS devices. For Windows, administrators can create condition groups using multiple conditions based on revision and build number. For Android, iOS, and macOS, compliance is evaluated by comparing the device OS version against a specified version using a selected operator.
b. Application Version: Generate reports for single or multiple applications across Android, iOS, Windows, and macOS. Administrators can group up to five application conditions in a single report.
c. Encryption Status: Generate compliance reports for Windows and macOS devices based on their encryption status.
d. Saved Compliance Reports: Save compliance report configurations as reusable filters to avoid repeatedly defining the same conditions. Up to 25 reports can be saved and shared across administrators.
e. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Compliance Reports now have dedicated RBAC permissions. Administrators with read/write access can save, edit, and delete reports, while other administrators can view reports and use saved filters.
f. DeepDive Integration: A new Compliance Overview section in DeepDive displays saved compliance reports graphically when enabled. Compliance is evaluated daily based on the conditions defined in each report, and the corresponding graphs are displayed.
2. OneIdP Conditional Access Enhancement for ChromeOS
Conditional Access settings in OneIdP now allow IT Administrators to block access to the service from ChromeOS devices.
Team
Team Scalefusion

new.title: October 21st, 2026
new.text:
Enhancement: Start Browser Discovery from Managed Devices or Third-Party MDM
Feature: AI & SaaS Management
Browser discovery in AI & SaaS Management can now start when a user signs in to a JumpCloud-managed device associated with them, or when you deploy the JumpCloud Go extension through a third-party MDM provider.
Use the path that matches how you manage devices and identity:
JumpCloud-managed devices: Tracking can start after a user signs in to a JumpCloud-managed device associated with them.
Third-party MDM: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from Settings, add them to the JumpCloud Go extension distribution policy, and deploy that policy. Discovery can start after the extension is installed. Discovery data is associated with a user after they sign in to the User Portal or a JumpCloud SSO application, or after they sign in to a JumpCloud-managed device associated with them.
See Get Started: AI & SaaS Management and Deploy JumpCloud Go Extension for SaaS Discovery with Third-Party MDM to learn more.

changed.title: October 14th, 2026
changed.text:
New: Agent Uninstall Protection
Feature: Device Management
Prevent unauthorized removal of the JumpCloud agent so your devices stay managed. Agent Uninstall Protection is on by default for all devices running JumpCloud agent v2.179.2 or later. Uninstalling the agent with standard methods on macOS, Windows, and Linux now requires a per-device maintenance token.
Directory Insights Events: Directory Insights logs failed uninstall attempts, successful uninstalls, and exemption policy changes, identifying the device and the user.
Maintenance Tokens: Admins with Manager role permissions or higher can view a device's maintenance token from the device details. Tokens work without network connectivity and automatically rotate 60 minutes after they're viewed if the agent remains installed.
Exemption Policies: Use the Disable Agent Uninstall Protection policy for macOS, Windows, or Linux to remove the token requirement from specific devices during agent maintenance, troubleshooting, or imaging.
Protection Status: View each device's protection status (On, Off, or Failed) from the device details or the Devices list.
Deleting an active device from the Admin Portal or the JumpCloud API still removes the agent without a maintenance token.
Available in the Admin Portal: Go to Device Management > Devices > Settings > Agent Uninstall Protection.
Learn More
Get Started: Agent Uninstall Protection
Create a Device Level macOS Disable Agent Uninstall Protection Policy
Create a Device Level Windows Disable Agent Uninstall Protection Policy
Create a Device Level Linux Disable Agent Uninstall Protection Policy
Install or Uninstall the JumpCloud Agent
Enhancement: Customize Email and Automation Variables tabs in Settings
Feature: Admin Portal
You'll see a refreshed look on the Customize Email and Automation Variables tabs, with shorter labels and helper text that's easier to scan. Your settings work exactly as before. They're just easier to find and update.
See Settings in the Admin Portal to learn more.
